claims.claim: Observed configuration: two H200 replicas use TP1/DP4 with expert parallelism, consistent with the user-stated EP4 topology. This is not the TP8 configuration used in most supplied benchmarks.
claims.conditions: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision 2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027; max-num-seqs 64; max-model-len 1,048,576; FP8 KV cache; block size 64; DSpark with five speculative tokens; prefix caching enabled.
claims.reported_result: The inventory records configuration and healthy endpoints. It contains no new GPU performance experiment.
claims.transfer_inference: Use the user-specified TP1 64-attention-head baseline. DP4/EP4 does not imply the 8 or 16 local attention heads of TP8/TP4. The configured sequence limit does not establish actual per-rank decode rows, and the maximum context does not establish the workload's context distribution.
claims.limitations: Actual per-rank concurrency, speculative row counts, compressed context lengths, indexer head shapes, active kernels, TPOT and sustainable capacity are unknown.

claims.quote: Planner launches per decode step drop from 21 to 4.
claims.claim: Author explanation: per-group plan holders duplicate FlashMLA planning despite existing reuse across same-type layers. Sharing holders across compatible KV groups removes redundant serial planner launches.
claims.conditions: Eight H20 96 GB GPUs, TP8/EP8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with five speculative tokens and synthetic mean acceptance length 3.51. Decode serving tests used 1K input/1K output at concurrency 1 and 64.
claims.reported_result: Author-reported profiling: 21 to 4 planner launches per step. Serving: output throughput improved 2.5% at C1 and 0.5% at C64; median ITL decreased 2.6% and 0.6%, respectively. Prefill TTFT was essentially unchanged.
claims.transfer_inference: This addresses redundant planning rather than small-head padding, so TP1 does not inherently exclude it. Selection depends on whether the live runner builds compatible groups separately and actually repeats planning.
claims.limitations: B3 was one run; the C64 effect was small relative to variation between baseline runs. V1 callers without the shared dictionary retain per-group plans; drafter and DBO passes remain separate. SM100 mega attention does not use this path. H200 launch counts, effect size and accuracy results are unknown; the supplied excerpt gives an accuracy protocol but no result. H20 ITL is not H200 TPOT.

claims.claim: Observed implementation: a dictionary local to build_attn_metadata shares plan holders using block size, causality and decode SWA width. Safe reuse additionally depends on equal live decode-length values across participating groups.
claims.conditions: Groups must belong to the same metadata-building pass and have compatible batch, window, valid-token mask, replay_start, topk_length and extra_topk_length values.
claims.reported_result: The supplied patch establishes the per-pass cache and sharing mechanism. It provides no independent execution or correctness result.
claims.transfer_inference: Shape equality alone is insufficient evidence for safe plan sharing. The live H200 path must preserve the value-equality invariant during eager execution and graph replay; reuse must not escape the intended pass.
claims.limitations: Actual H200 group composition and replay invariants are unknown. Installed excerpts already show same-type plan reuse, but do not establish whether cross-group sharing is absent or how many redundant launches remain.

claims.claim: Observed implementation: the gather kernel copies candidate FP8 K payloads and their FP32 scales from paged storage into a compact workspace. The module describes scoring that workspace with the existing non-paged kernel, then applying top-k and remapping.
claims.conditions: Candidate-consuming decode indexers with compatible paged FP8 cache layout and valid candidate indices. Candidate-source and pre-candidate layers have no candidate set to exploit.
claims.reported_result: The supplied code establishes the gather mechanism and default-off environment controls. Its comments explicitly allow numerical or selected-index differences from different scoring kernels and tie-breaking.
claims.transfer_inference: This replaces full compressed-context scoring followed by candidate masking. It is an alternative to #62463's direct paged scoring, not an additional stage to stack with it.
claims.limitations: The patch excerpt is truncated before the complete dispatch and scoring integration. H200 workspace cost, indexer-shape compatibility, latency and model accuracy are unknown. The approximately 98% discarded-work figure is an author estimate for a long-context regime, not an observed H200 fraction.

claims.claim: Author-reported measurements support candidate gathering as a way to reduce consumer-indexer work at long context and sufficient decode rows.
claims.conditions: Eight H20 GPUs, TP8, DSv4.1, approximately 1M context, nine concurrent requests and five speculative tokens: approximately 54 flattened decode rows. Scope is SM90, FP8 indexer cache and no context parallelism.
claims.reported_result: Profiler-derived time for four consumer indexers decreased from 9.57 to 3.05 ms per step; total step time decreased from 39.04 to 31.53 ms. Selected top-k sets reportedly matched the dense path on tested identical inputs.
claims.transfer_inference: The relevant predictor is local rows times scanned compressed context relative to candidate width. TP8 request concurrency cannot be mapped directly onto either TP1/DP4 H200 replica.
claims.limitations: Profiler-free serving A/B, independent numerical reference, model-level accuracy and other-SM90 validation were pending. Set equivalence is weaker than bit-identical scores or outputs. H200 effect size is unknown.

claims.claim: Strong counterevidence: gathering regressed at one request even in the tested long-context workload, and its workload-dependent host dispatch becomes fixed under full CUDA graph capture.
claims.conditions: The single-request case contributes approximately six decode rows with five speculative tokens. Candidate gathering has a fixed per-step cost; default workload gates impose only minimal shape bounds.
claims.reported_result: The author reports approximately 11.6% slower single-request steps. The feature remains default-off; graph-aware selection and automatic small-batch protection are unfinished.
claims.transfer_inference: Retain dense scoring as a serious comparator at short contexts and low row counts. The example MIN_ROWS=16 is not an established H200 crossover. Capture-time path freezing is a dispatch/performance limitation; by itself it does not prove incorrect logits.
claims.limitations: The H200 crossover is unknown. Passing gather/replay tests does not establish a correct adaptive selection policy. FORCE bypasses workload gates rather than proving profitability. Dense fallback for unsupported configurations does not guarantee protection for every supported but unprofitable workload.

claims.claim: Implementation evidence supports a different design: score candidate K directly through the page table, write compact logits, run existing top-k and remap. The visible preparation kernel derives causal row limits from device-resident sequence lengths.
claims.conditions: Intended for SM90 candidate-consuming FP8 decode indexers. For request-level lengths, speculative row s uses max(base - next_n + 1 + s, 0). The interface includes live page tables and causal bounds.
claims.reported_result: Observed code establishes device-side row-bound preparation and a direct paged-scoring interface. Module documentation describes eliminating the intermediate candidate-K copy and avoiding context-dependent host dispatch.
claims.transfer_inference: This directly addresses the gather prototype's extra K-copy stage and capture-time workload decision. Compare #62463 and #62000 separately against dense scoring; their gains cannot be added. A correct fixed graph path can still be slower than dense at short contexts.
claims.limitations: The excerpt ends before the complete scoring body and eligibility checks. Full architecture, cache-layout and shape gates cannot be independently audited from this excerpt. Graph-live-length correctness is partly implementation evidence and partly author-described design, not a new verified H200 result.

claims.quote:
All eight ranks
show the new kernel
claims.claim: Author-reported serving and trace evidence shows that direct paged candidate scoring was exercised and improved ITL in the measured H20 long-context cases.
claims.conditions: Eight H20 96 GB GPUs, TP8, five speculative tokens, prefix caching enabled; 1,029,974 measured input tokens and 16,384 output tokens per request. Serving concurrency was 1/2/4/8.
claims.reported_result: Mean ITL decreased 9.6–23.8% across those concurrency points. Consumer logits used 16,384 candidate columns. A separate C12 trace showed the new kernel on all ranks and removal of consumer mask kernels.
claims.transfer_inference: Direct paged scoring is a plausible long-context integration candidate because it removes discarded scoring without copying candidate K. Unlike small-head attention kernels, its applicability cannot be decided from attention-head count alone; the actual indexer shape must be checked.
claims.limitations: These are H20 TP8 observations, not H200 TP1 predictions. Candidate-source layers, pre-candidate layers and prefill remain unchanged. Neither the reported ITL reduction nor trace attribution establishes H200 TPOT or capacity.

claims.quote: This is one A/B pair, not a confidence-interval result.
claims.claim: Strong counterevidence limits both performance confidence and readiness: the serving sample is tiny, throughput does not improve everywhere, and model accuracy and shorter-workload checks remain pending.
claims.conditions: One run per configuration, with only 2/4/8/16 measured requests at C1/2/4/8. Shared-prefix workload, changing speculative acceptance, and a separate profiler comparison with different batches.
claims.reported_result: At C4, overall completion throughput fell from 827.33 to 814.72 tok/s, or 1.5%, despite lower ITL. The earlier TP4/200K test had a much smaller, unquantified ITL change. Profiler rows averaged 55.2 versus 44.3, and the dense scoring bucket included source plus consumer layers.
claims.transfer_inference: Do not treat the scoring-call timings as a matched-load speedup or the ITL results as a universal serving win. Configuration-based dispatch avoids frozen context thresholds, but does not establish a profitable short-context fallback. Acceptance, scheduling and buffering prevent equating streamed ITL with GPU iteration time or TPOT.
claims.limitations: Model accuracy is pending. Tests are described for FP32-reference scores, selected sets, causal bounds and changed-length/page-table replay, but SM90 cases are skipped by L4 CI and a saved H20 test report is still needed. Client cache counters do not establish server-side prefix-cache behavior. Independent repetitions and H200 results are unknown.

The actually selected cooperative, persistent or per-row backend, extension build targets and runtime activation are unknown. The candidate consumer's 16,384-column buffer is also below the 128K cluster threshold. Dense and compact-logit top-k need separate comparisons.

claims.quote: SM90, 8 or 16 local heads, decode only
claims.claim: Author explanation: TP8/TP4 leaves 8/16 attention heads padded to a 64-head WGMMA tile. A 16-head Triton tile with split-key reduction removes padding work at low decode-row counts. This mechanism does not match the TP1 64-head baseline.
claims.conditions: Dispatch requires 8 or 16 local heads. It allows at most 16 decode tokens for key widths <=256, or 12 for larger compressed layers tested with top-k 512. Serving tests used eight H20 GPUs, TP8 and DSpark K=2.
claims.reported_result: Author-reported median ITL reductions were 5.7–9.9% at C1–4. For compressed attention, running the kernel outside its gate produced 0.90–0.94x speedups at 16–32 tokens. GSM8K changed from 1187 to 1186 correct out of 1319, with answer flips in both directions.
claims.transfer_inference: Exclude this padding-removal mechanism from the unchanged TP1 64-head baseline. Neither EP4 nor DP4 creates the small local head count. seq64 is a configured sequence limit, not this kernel's per-step token gate.
claims.limitations: Larger batches become gather/dequantization-bound. Results used a patched vLLM 0.30.0 image rather than the exact PR head; CI and interleaved serving repetitions were pending. H200 effects are unknown, and the reported H20 ITL cannot be imported as H200 TPOT.

claims.claim: Author explanation: native 8/16/32-head sparse prefill avoids padding TP-local queries to 64 heads. The existing 64-head path is a control, not the source of the reported small-head gains.
claims.conditions: SM90 sparse prefill; QK dimensions 512/576; one KV head; actual head count must be passed. Strided head slices, attention sink, per-query lengths and LSE semantics are described.
claims.reported_result: The author reports 155 H20 tests and 63 sanitizer boundary cases passing. The displayed 64-head controls are approximately 1.000–1.004x, while small-head configurations show larger gains.
claims.transfer_inference: This does not justify a prefill speedup for the TP1 64-head baseline. A TP change would be a separate deployment decision. It also does not establish FP8 decode improvement.
claims.limitations: Kernel implementation is described but its patch body is not supplied. H200 performance is unknown. The page repeats the integration benchmark from #61615, so those numbers are not independent replication.

claims.quote: Preserve padding for FP8 decode and other architectures.
claims.claim: Author claim: passing actual TP-local heads activates small-head sparse prefill through FlashMLA #26 while preserving the existing FP8 decode behavior.
claims.conditions: TP4 serving test; 128 requests; concurrency 32; 4096 input and 128 output tokens; DSpark with five speculative tokens; prefix caching disabled. The supplied serving excerpt does not identify GPU hardware.
claims.reported_result: Output throughput increased from 365.65 to 393.10 tok/s; mean TPOT decreased from 68.92 to 64.19 ms. P99 TPOT increased from 137.52 to 140.59 ms, and speculative acceptance changed from 48.57% to 46.68%.
claims.transfer_inference: These are TP4 small-head integration results, not evidence for TP1 64-head gains. The mixed tail results and changing acceptance also limit attributing every serving change to prefill.
claims.limitations: Serving hardware, repeated-run variability and model-accuracy results are unknown in the supplied excerpt. An evaluation command is not an accuracy result. The identical benchmark reproduced in FlashMLA #26 must not be counted twice.

claims.claim: Author proposal: prepack selected attention KV records to remove page translation and irregular gathers from the attention stage. Strong counterevidence is that including unhidden packing makes the measured path slower.
claims.conditions: Reported NVIDIA L20X with 132 SMs; SM90; V3.2 FP8 656-byte KV records; d_qk=576, d_v=512; H=64/128; top-k 2048; 60 batch/query configurations. This is attention-KV packing, distinct from #62000's indexer-K gather.
claims.reported_result: Attention alone achieved 1.098x geometric-mean speedup with an identical scheduler. Pack plus attention without overlap achieved only 0.740x and won none of 60 cases. Five correctness cases reportedly passed.
claims.transfer_inference: Matching H=64 alone does not establish applicability to the live V4.1 cache format. Selection would depend on compatible records, an actual overlap window and correct current-token updates. EP communication is only a possible overlap opportunity, not measured evidence.
claims.limitations: Runtime orchestration, stream synchronization, current-token updates and end-to-end TPOT are absent. Workspace is approximately 1.281 MiB per query row at top-k 2048. Host offload and capacity expansion are explicitly outside the PR. SM100 is excluded; H200 compatibility, benefit and capacity effect are unknown.

claims.quote: only those heads run the heavy token-level scoring.
claims.claim: Abstract-level author proposal: MISA routes a subset of indexer heads to reduce token-scoring work. This is algorithmic head selection, distinct from TP padding removal and candidate-only scoring.
claims.conditions: The supplied abstract discusses DSA and gives DeepSeek-V3.2's 64 indexer heads as an example. These are not evidence for the live V4.1 attention or indexer shapes.
claims.reported_result: No usable experimental result or implementation is present in the supplied excerpt.

claims.limitations: Hardware, workload, effect size, implementation, accuracy and relevant limitations are unknown. The fulltext_available metadata does not make the missing experimental body available as evidence.

unanswered: What are the live per-rank decode-row distribution, compressed context lengths, candidate widths, indexer head dimensions and top-k values? seq64 and a 1M maximum context do not answer these selection questions.
Does the installed runner already share plans across groups, and how many duplicate planner launches occur on H200? Without that profile, the remaining opportunity for #58818 is unknown.
Do every participating group's live top-k/SWA lengths, masks and replay_start remain equal when sharing plans, including during graph replay?
What are the complete architecture and shape gates for both candidate implementations? The supplied patch excerpts are insufficient to audit all eligibility branches.
Where does dense scoring beat gather or direct paged scoring on H200, especially at short contexts and one request? #62000 reports a regression; #62463 has no completed short-workload evidence.

Do candidate scoring and remapping preserve required numerical, causal, invalid-entry and model-accuracy behavior on H200 under changed graph-live lengths and page tables? Described tests and top-k set comparisons do not establish all of these.

Which top-k backend actually runs today, and how does an SM90 FP32 DeepSelect build compare against it for both dense-width and 16,384-column candidate logits? Build availability, dispatch, alignment and performance remain unknown.

Would repeated, matched H200 serving runs improve TPOT distributions, completion throughput and SLO-constrained capacity after controlling acceptance, prefix caching and scheduling? No new GPU experiment exists.
What exactly were the old B200 exclusions? Their record is not supplied. Current sources establish mechanism-specific SM90/SM100 restrictions, but cannot validate historical exclusion decisions.
Can selected-KV packing match the live V4.1 format and hide enough packing cost without stale current-token data or excessive workspace? No supplied runtime integration establishes this.
The supplied MISA excerpt omits implementation and experiments; its hardware applicability, accuracy tradeoff and effect size cannot influence selection beyond conceptual context.
